C-DROPBOX-SCOPE-DIAGNOSTICS.Summary: Recognize modern Dropbox missing-scope responses within the approved save/load correction.
C-DROPBOX-SCOPE-DIAGNOSTICS.Problem: The saved token passes a live read-only check/user request, while files/download returns HTTP 400 with a required-scope error. The handler requires an exact legacy sentence prefix and hides the useful explanation behind a request ID.

Goals.Goal: Recognize required-scope errors regardless of provider app-ID wording and report the required endpoint permission.
Keep the provider response body and credentials private.

Constraints.Constraint: Preserve upload/download request contracts, encrypted credentials, PKCE, atomic restore, and existing UI behavior.
Automated verification uses simulated responses and temporary databases; live read-only diagnosis is separate from tests.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Change Dropbox App Console permissions or use the account for an upload.
Infer the specific upload rejection reason solely from a request ID.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Documented legacy authorization failures and modern required-scope responses produce App Console submission and relinking guidance for the correct file permission.
Tests cover app-ID wording, JSON/plain-text errors, unrelated 400 responses, secrecy, and absence of automatic retries.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Deterministic permission-error variants and sanitized fallback evidence without live credentials.

Assumptions.Assumption: The existing explicit approval of save/load execution and its HTTP permission diagnostics covers this correction to the same handler.
The read-only live check found missing file-read scope; App Console permission submission and fresh consent are external steps for the user.
